Looping you all in to draft a concise recommendation for Priya. Key constraints: 80 rps typical, bursts to 120, P95 < 400ms, large nightly long-context rerank (8k tokens). Cost sensitivity: moderate.

Quick notes/asks for internal:
- Dev: can you run a micro-benchmark showing average tokens/sec and latency for our three SKU families (H100 80GB, A100 40GB, L4 24GB) across two payload types: short-gen (120 tokens) and long-context rerank (8k tokens)? Include expected concurrency per GPU for each workload.
- Rishi: ops considerations — disk/memory footprint for KV cache, expected slow-path swap behavior for long contexts on A100 vs H100, and whether we should advise reserving burst pool (hosted burst) or bake into Dedicated.
- Marcus: update the cost model spreadsheet with per-hour cost assumptions for reserved vs on-demand for each SKU and a 3-month pilot cost.
- Lauren: craft a customer-facing 1-page recommendation that explains tradeoffs in plain language for procurement.

I drafted an initial fleet mix below (very rough — objective is predictability and keeping latency under SLO):
- Production user-facing (real-time): primarily L4s for cost-effective low-latency generation; L4 provides fast inference for short sequences and low token budgets.
- Heavy long-context / batch rerank: H100s (80GB) to fit 8k token contexts on-device and avoid performance cliffs.
- Mid-tier / model-compatibility: A100s as a flexible buffer for legacy or finetuned models that need more memory than L4 but are not long-context heavy.

Ballpark baseline Reserved suggestion (pilot):
- 20 x L4 (handle steady-state web traffic with batching, KV cache, and low-latency path)
- 4 x H100 (nightly rerank + overflow for long-context requests)
- 6 x A100 (can soak medium concurrent workloads and provide fallbacks)

Pros/cons to call out:
- H100: best for long contexts and large batch reranks; highest per-unit cost but reduces engineering complexity for the rerank job.
- A100: good middle ground; cheaper than H100 (depending on reservation) but may require sharding or clever chunking for 8k contexts. Watch for slower KV swap and potential swap to host for >40GB models.
- L4: lowest cost per token for short generations; excellent for high-concurrency web traffic, but limited for long-context or proprietary huge-fine-tuned models.

I'll consolidate Dev/Rishi/Marcus inputs and send a customer-ready note. Action: Dev please share benchmark numbers by Thu 26th.

— Evelyn

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity planning for Zenith pilot — micro-benchmarks

Attached are micro-benchmarks (summary below) — ran on representative model variants and measured throughput and P95 latency under simulated request mixes. Details in sheet "bench-summary" of the attached workbook.

Summary (short-gen: 120 tokens; long-context: 8k tokens):
- L4 (24GB): short-gen
  - Sustained throughput (single GPU): ~900 tokens/sec usable when batching; per-request P95 ~120-180ms at 80 RPS with our batching settings. Concurrency per GPU for SLO: ~40-60 concurrent short-gen requests depending on batching window.
- A100 (40GB): short-gen & medium contexts
  - Short-gen throughput comparable to L4 but with better variability; can host some finetuned mid-size models. For 8k token context, needs sharding or chunking; per-request P95 for short-gen ~140-220ms under similar load.
- H100 (80GB): long-context
  - Handles 8k token context without sharding; batch rerank throughput (for the nightly job) ~3-4 documents/sec per GPU for large contexts depending on model. Per-request P95 for short-gen slightly worse than L4 at same batching, but within acceptable limits when traffic is routed preferentially to L4.

Observations:
- L4 provides the best per-token economics for the user-facing workload and keeps P95 well under 400ms when routed correctly.
- A100 is a good fallback for models that need larger memory than L4 but aren't full long-context jobs. Expect engineering overhead to split long contexts across two A100s if we go that route.
- H100 is the only practical single-GPU option for 8k token reranks without sharding; reduces orchestration complexity for the nightly batch.

I included a simple model for expected GPU utilization and estimated reserved counts (sheet: "reserved-proposal").

— Dev

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity planning for Zenith pilot — ops notes

Ops notes to include in the customer-facing doc and in the contract:
- KV cache sizing: estimate ~120GB aggregated working set for the short-gen production fleet under expected prefix reuse; that comfortably fits on L4s when we shard appropriately, but plan for a small NVMe fallback cache.
- Persistent storage: nightly rerank artifacts and logs should be offloaded to S3-compatible storage; don't rely on local disk for replayability.
- Burst capacity: recommend a small hosted burst bucket (on-demand) for short-term peaks (allows us to reserve smaller Dedicated footprint). We should include a clear fallback policy in the SLA: route to hosted L4s (higher cost) when Dedicated pool is saturated.
- Upgrade path: if Zenith expands context lengths in future, recommend phasing in H100s as primary long-context workers and migrating rerank to dedicated H100 cluster.
- Security/compliance: Zen wants SOC2 docs — I'll attach standard evidence and offer SOC2-in-scope deployment notes.

Operational risk: the biggest engineering lift will be orchestration of long-context rerank if we try to force-fit it onto A100s with chunking — increases failure modes and complicates debugging.

— Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Head of Production Engineering
